summary: Defined a frontend-only landing-page refresh that applies the supplied visual mood to OncoReady's existing product story, integrates the official logo assets, and adds one bounded pointer-reactive continuity visual without changing workflow behavior.
decisions: Treat the Lovable/Invofy material as mood and style inspiration only; preserve OncoReady's information architecture, content, functional destinations, healthcare context, and official brand.

Integrate the official title-logo and favicon assets from the repository Logo directory through the frontend public asset pipeline, with full and compact responsive variants rather than recreating the wordmark in HTML text.

Keep the completed CORE-001 workflow, role entry, readiness preview, FAQ behavior, and client-side navigation authoritative; the visual refresh may change presentation and supporting copy but not workflow or routing semantics.

Use one isolated signature continuity visual inspired by the supplied character-form references. It may use canvas, SVG, or DOM characters, but it must remain decorative, have a static reduced-motion presentation, pause offscreen/when hidden, and never gate content or navigation.

Prefer existing React, TypeScript, Tailwind, and motion capabilities with no new dependency. Any custom render loop must bound device-pixel ratio and work per frame and avoid layout reads within the loop.
Remove or rewrite unsupported absolute outcome language while preserving a confident product voice and the primary treatment-readiness story.
Limit scope to the public landing experience plus shared logo/header/footer compatibility; do not restyle the operational portals or change shared workflow state in this slice.
Use existing frontend state and event handlers directly. No formal contract is required because there is no independently implemented component or external API boundary.

risks.description: A pointer-reactive character field could reduce performance or create discomfort on mobile and motion-sensitive devices.
risks.mitigation: Use a bounded effect with a static fallback, reduced-motion equivalence, offscreen and hidden-page pausing, capped resolution/particle count, and mobile verification.

risks.description: A strong external reference could lead to an imitation that weakens OncoReady's identity or imports irrelevant SaaS marketing patterns.
risks.mitigation: Bind the design to the official OncoReady assets, brand tokens, treatment-readiness narrative, readiness graph, and current information architecture; explicitly exclude copied testimonials, logo marquees, imagery, copy, and component structure.

risks.description: Landing-page restructuring could break entry into the completed Maria workflow or existing anchor navigation.
risks.mitigation: Preserve current callbacks and state ownership, keep the animation independent of workflow state, and exercise landing entry plus the existing critical journey in smoke verification.

risks.description: The official horizontal wordmark may become unreadable or distorted at small widths.
risks.mitigation: Use explicit responsive full and compact logo variants with correct aspect ratios, intrinsic sizing, accessible names, and layout-shift-safe dimensions.

notes_for_next_agent: Codex must perform design Phase A before production frontend changes because this materially changes landing composition, identity expression, and motion; the human explicitly assigned Codex as frontend owner for this task.
The human explicitly wants only the reference's color, theme, and style as inspiration, not its overall design or information architecture.
Inspect all repository-provided UI Suggestion images and official Logo assets during Phase A; the local files are authoritative references for this task.
Keep exact aesthetic choices within the approved Phase A design while satisfying the confirmed official-brand, light/clear, captivating-but-calm, and one-signature-motion constraints.

Candidate implementation areas are LandingPage, Header, Logo, shared public UI/decorations, index styles/tokens, frontend public assets, and focused smoke checks. Avoid workflow-state changes unless a concrete compatibility issue is reported.
Do not add testimonials, customer-logo claims, unsupported pricing/outcome claims, or imply live hospital integrations merely because the reference includes those marketing patterns.
SMOKE depth is implementation-owned; no independent tester or security reviewer is selected.
